_link.title: I can explain long-term potentiation, including the structural changes it produces at the neural synapse

toLevel2.answer: The long-lasting strengthening of synaptic connections
distractors: The temporary weakening of synaptic connections
The removal of unused neural pathway connections
The creation of entirely new neurons in the brain

toLevel2.stem: Which neurotransmitter drives the repeated stimulation of the postsynaptic neuron during LTP?
distractors: Serotonin
Dopamine
GABA

toLevel2.stem: Which of the following is one of the three structural changes produced by LTP?
toLevel2.answer: Increased number of receptor sites on dendrites
distractors: Decreased number of synaptic vesicles released
Reduced number of connections between all neurons
Thinner dendrites due to loss of neural branching

toLevel2.stem: What causes dendrites to become bushier during LTP?
distractors: Pruning
Rerouting
Inhibition

toLevel2.stem: How many structural changes does LTP produce at the neural synapse?
distractors: One
Two
Four

toLevel2.stem: Long-term potentiation involves the long-lasting strengthening of synaptic connections that are regularly coactivated.
distractors: False

toLevel2.stem: Long-term potentiation produces a decreased number of receptor sites on the postsynaptic neuron's dendrites.
distractors: True

toLevel2.stem: LTP is driven by increased {{blank:1}} release, which produces repeated high-intensity stimulation of the postsynaptic neuron.

distractors: serotonin
dopamine

toLevel2.stem: The three structural changes produced by LTP are increased receptor sites, {{blank:1}} dendrites, and increased synaptic connections.

distractors: thinner
shorter

toLevel2.stem: Long-term potentiation is the {{blank:1}} of synaptic connections that are regularly coactivated through experience.

distractors: weakening
elimination

toLevel3.stem: Why does LTP explain how practice improves performance?
toLevel3.answer: Repeated activation strengthens the relevant synaptic connections
distractors: Practice creates entirely new neurons for each repetition
Practice reduces the number of connections to improve speed
Repeated activation weakens distracting neural pathways only

toLevel3.stem: How does an increased number of receptor sites on dendrites contribute to stronger synaptic connections?
toLevel3.answer: More receptor sites allow more neurotransmitter to bind
distractors: More receptor sites reduce the amount of neurotransmitter released
More receptor sites prevent the neuron from firing action potentials
More receptor sites cause the synaptic cleft to become much wider

toLevel3.stem: Why is glutamate specifically important in the process of LTP?
toLevel3.answer: It is the excitatory neurotransmitter that stimulates the postsynaptic neuron
distractors: It inhibits the postsynaptic neuron to prevent overstimulation
It removes unused connections to make the pathway more efficient
It is the only neurochemical present in the synaptic cleft region

toLevel3.stem: How does sprouting contribute to LTP?
toLevel3.answer: It creates bushier dendrites and more synaptic connections
distractors: It removes unused connections to streamline the neural pathway
It redirects signals away from the potentiated synaptic pathway
It decreases the number of receptor sites on the postsynaptic neuron

toLevel3.stem: Why do exam questions require students to name specific structural changes rather than just saying 'connections strengthen'?
toLevel3.answer: Naming specific changes demonstrates precise understanding
distractors: There is only one structural change, so specificity is easy
Saying connections strengthen is always sufficient for marks
Structural changes are not actually part of the LTP process

toLevel3.stem: What is the relationship between LTP and synaptic plasticity?
toLevel3.answer: LTP is one form of synaptic plasticity that strengthens connections
distractors: LTP and synaptic plasticity are identical interchangeable terms
LTP opposes synaptic plasticity by preventing any neural change
Synaptic plasticity only occurs through LTP and no other process

toLevel3.stem: LTP explains why repeated practice of a skill makes performance faster and more efficient, as the relevant synaptic connections are strengthened.
distractors: False

toLevel3.stem: LTP explains learning because repeated activation of a pathway causes its synaptic connections to become {{blank:1}}, making transmission more efficient.

distractors: weaker
slower

toLevel3.stem: An increased number of receptor sites means more {{blank:1}} can bind to the postsynaptic neuron, making the connection more responsive.

distractors: electrical charge
synaptic vesicles

toLevel3.stem: LTP is one form of {{blank:1}} that strengthens connections, while long-term depression is the form that weakens them.

distractors: receptor specificity
synaptic transmission

toLevel4.stem: Ava practises typing on a new keyboard layout daily for two months and notices her typing speed has improved. Which structural change best explains this improvement?
toLevel4.answer: Increased receptor sites and bushier dendrites in relevant pathways
distractors: Decreased receptor sites and thinner dendrites in motor regions
Removal of all existing connections and creation of new neurons
Weakened synaptic connections across the entire cerebral cortex

toLevel4.stem: A neuroscientist examines brain tissue from a person who practised violin for 20 years. Which finding would be most consistent with LTP?
toLevel4.answer: Bushier dendrites in motor regions associated with finger movement
distractors: Fewer synaptic connections in motor regions of the brain cortex
Reduced number of receptor sites on postsynaptic neuron dendrites
Thinner dendrites throughout all regions of the cerebral cortex

toLevel4.stem: Jake studies for his psychology exam by reviewing notes every evening for three weeks. Which explanation of his improved recall best applies LTP?
toLevel4.answer: Repeated activation increased receptor sites and synaptic connections
distractors: New neurons were created each time he reviewed his study notes
His brain removed unused connections to make recall more focused
Glutamate levels decreased so fewer signals reached his neurons

toLevel4.stem: A student writes: 'LTP occurs because connections get stronger.' A teacher asks them to be more specific. Which response best applies knowledge of LTP?
toLevel4.answer: Receptor sites increase, dendrites become bushier, and new connections form
distractors: Neurons grow larger cell bodies and produce more electrical current
The synaptic cleft widens to allow more neurotransmitter to travel
Motor neurons replace interneurons in the relevant brain pathway

toLevel4.stem: Mia has been learning to play chess for six months and finds she can now recognise patterns much faster. Which LTP-related change in her brain best accounts for this?
toLevel4.answer: Strengthened connections due to increased receptor sites and sprouting
distractors: Weakened connections from reduced glutamate at relevant synapses
New neurons created specifically for chess pattern recognition
Removal of all unrelated connections from her brain's visual area

toLevel4.stem: A researcher measures glutamate levels in participants before and after an intensive language course. Which result would be most consistent with LTP occurring?
toLevel4.answer: Increased glutamate activity in language-related brain regions
distractors: Decreased glutamate activity across all regions of the brain
No change in glutamate activity in any measured brain areas
Glutamate replaced by GABA in the language processing regions

toLevel4.stem: Tom is asked to explain why his guitar playing improved after months of practice. Which answer correctly applies all three structural changes of LTP?
toLevel4.answer: More receptor sites, bushier dendrites, and more synaptic connections formed
distractors: Fewer receptor sites, thinner dendrites, and fewer synaptic connections
New neurons were created, old neurons were destroyed, and GABA increased
The synaptic cleft widened, vesicles decreased, and glutamate was removed

toLevel4.stem: When Ava practises typing daily, LTP in her motor pathways produces {{blank:1}} dendrites and an increased number of {{blank:2}} on the postsynaptic neuron.

distractors: thinner
shorter
synaptic vesicles
axon terminals

toLevel4.stem: Jake's improved exam recall after three weeks of revision is explained by LTP, which was driven by increased {{blank:1}} release at the relevant synapses.

distractors: serotonin
dopamine

toLevel4.stem: A student who writes that 'connections get stronger' during LTP should specify the three structural changes: increased receptor sites, bushier dendrites, and increased {{blank:1}}.

distractors: electrical impulses
neuron cell bodies

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that LTP can occur without glutamate because other neurotransmitters can also stimulate neurons. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: At VCE level, glutamate is the neurotransmitter driving LTP
distractors: Correct; any neurotransmitter can drive LTP equally well
Correct; glutamate has no specific role in LTP at all
Incorrect; LTP does not involve any neurotransmitter release

toLevel5.stem: Dr Chen argues that simply saying 'synaptic connections strengthen' is sufficient to explain LTP in a VCE exam. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Insufficient; specific structural changes must be named for full marks
distractors: Correct; naming structural changes is unnecessary for any exam marks
Correct; examiners only require a general description of strengthening
Insufficient; but only one structural change needs to be identified

toLevel5.stem: A student writes that LTP produces 'more neurons in the brain.' Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; LTP changes existing connections, not the number of neurons
distractors: Correct; LTP creates new neurons through cell division processes
Correct; more neurons are always the result of strengthened pathways
Incorrect; LTP destroys neurons rather than creating new ones

toLevel5.stem: Emma argues that LTP makes learning permanent and irreversible. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; connections can weaken through long-term depression
distractors: Correct; once LTP occurs, the changes can never be reversed
Correct; all learning through LTP is permanent and irreversible
Incorrect; LTP does not contribute to any form of lasting learning

toLevel5.stem: A researcher claims that bushier dendrites are the most important structural change in LTP because they create the most new connections. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: All three structural changes contribute to LTP; ranking them is not supported
distractors: Correct; bushier dendrites are the only structural change that truly matters
Incorrect; receptor site increases are the only change that matters in LTP
Correct; the other two structural changes are irrelevant to the LTP process

toLevel5.stem: A student argues that LTP and synaptic plasticity are the same thing. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; LTP is one form of synaptic plasticity among others
distractors: Correct; LTP is the only form of plasticity that exists
Correct; synaptic plasticity and LTP are interchangeable terms
Incorrect; LTP and synaptic plasticity are completely unrelated

toLevel5.stem: Marcus claims that a single practice session is enough to produce the full structural changes of LTP. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Unlikely; LTP typically requires repeated stimulation over time
distractors: Correct; one intense session produces all three structural changes
Correct; repetition is unnecessary for any form of neural change
Incorrect; practice sessions cannot produce any structural changes

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that LTP only occurs in motor pathways because it relates to physical practice. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; LTP occurs in any pathway that is repeatedly activated
distractors: Correct; LTP is exclusive to motor regions of the brain cortex
Correct; cognitive learning does not involve LTP or any plasticity
Incorrect; LTP only occurs in sensory pathways, not motor pathways

toLevel5.stem: The claim that LTP creates new neurons is {{blank:1}} because LTP changes existing {{blank:2}} rather than producing new cells.

distractors: correct
plausible
neuronal cell bodies
brain tissue regions

toLevel5.stem: Saying 'connections strengthen' without naming the three structural changes is {{blank:1}} for a VCE exam because examiners require {{blank:2}}.

distractors: fully adequate
completely wrong
general summaries
personal opinions
